Shift quiet corners rules
New staff will learn how a new handler works

Page topic: safe intake, checking, and handoff for companion animals. This matters because a calm, correct first step keeps the traveler, the animal, and the ground team aligned from desk to cabin.

At the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, your first job is to slow the pace without losing control of the line. Listen to the passenger, look over the booking, and confirm the animal type, carrier condition, and any papers in hand. If Nora Costa arrives worried, or Theo Andersson looks rushed, keep your voice even and give clear directions. A steady answer at the counter prevents confusion later on the ramp.

For health documents and pet acceptance, use the current checklist every time. <<FACT F081>> If a traveler is unsure, do not guess; check the file, then move the case to the senior coordinator if anything does not match. Record only what the desk has confirmed, and keep your notes brief, clear, and readable for the next shift.

Carrier checks are simple but strict. Make sure the container is secure, clean, and fit for the species before you continue. <<FACT F070>> If the crate is too tight, damaged, or missing a working latch, stop the process and explain the issue without sounding sharp. The passenger may be frustrated, but your job is to stay firm and practical.

Fees and special handling also need direct attention. Some cases need a charge before acceptance. <<FACT F060>> Tell the traveler what happens next in plain language, then move the file forward only after the correct step is complete. If Winston is the pet at the counter, keep the focus on safety, not sympathy alone.

The ground team moves carriers carefully between services, and they rely on your notes being accurate. Supervisors listen carefully when a passenger is worried, so never hide a problem or soften a warning. Remember to stay calm, verify the facts, and hand off only when the animal, the papers, and the record all match.
